scope: Selected ADR reconsiderations for ISO 32000-2 §8.6.5.8, §10.5, and halftone TransferFunction entries only.

decisions.question: Map the four PDF rendering intents to ICC profile transforms, including unknown names.
decisions.source: §8.6.5.8 printed pp.196-197 / physical pp.211-212; Table 69; §10.3.1 is supporting ICC mapping outside full recertification. EC3 #63 strikes the note language that had excused support for the four standard intents.
decisions.assessment: Retain the four standard intent mappings and RelativeColorimetric fallback. Current tests use distinct profile transforms and exercise ri, ExtGState, image-local, default and unknown-name routes through CPU raster output. Do not describe the struck phrase as effective text or infer support obligations for extra device-specific names.

decisions.question: Apply transfer maps at rendering while permitting a continuous-tone device to ignore halftone screens.
decisions.source: §10.5 printed pp.364-365 / physical pp.379-380; §10.6.5.1 printed p.372 / physical p.387.
decisions.assessment: Retain the distinction: §10.6.5.1 permits ignoring screen behavior, while §10.5 still defines transfer mapping. Existing /TR raster tests show CPU consumption; direct HT override tests currently inspect maps via a helper rather than raster output. The draft supplies public-raster Type 5 and Type 6 controls.
decisions.status: interpretation supported; public HT assertion gap drafted

decisions.question: Treat halftone TransferFunction as a per-component override over the current graphics-state transfer.
decisions.source: §10.5 and Tables128–131: Type6 Table129 physical390–391; Type5 §10.6.5.6/Table132 physical395–397. #311 deletes the entire contrast paragraph on396.
decisions.assessment: Retain for sampled RGB primary components. Draft controls compare each override with the same valid screen lacking the override and exercise Type 6 stream dictionary extraction. EC3 #310 addresses Type 5 producer entries for nonprimary/nonstandard-primary components; it does not prove a reader rejection obligation. EC3 #311 removes the cited nonprimary fallback paragraph, so no such behavior is certified here.
decisions.status: supported for sampled RGB paths; residuals explicit

decisions.question: Halftone name resolution and screen dispatch.
decisions.source: §10.6 halftone screen tables and name-specific behavior, outside this TransferFunction audit except the continuous-tone ignore permission.
decisions.assessment: Not reconsidered. This shard does not certify screen generation, spot-function behavior, device-specific names, or raster threshold algorithms.

decisions.question: Halftone fallback and screen semantics.
decisions.source: §10.6 screen behavior; selected TransferFunction table entries are the only overlap reviewed.
decisions.assessment: No broader conclusion drawn from the TransferFunction evidence. Review only confirms that sampled transfer overrides are routed separately from screen rendering.
decisions.status: out of scope except noted overlap
